name: Marlowe May
life: “I still remember my first audit being off by one sweet.” People around Harbour Bakery know Marlowe by a small Thursday habit. Marlowe buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I manage a cashless shop. I want to know why the pencil line moved faster than ours.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a narrow-striped sweater and a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand. Marlowe has a small notch in the left eyebrow, with a dark undercut with a longer wave on top. Marlowe starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak during a conversation.
personality: Marlowe listens for the familiar version of a story and then for the one detail that changes it. Friends bring problems here when they want to be heard twice.
agenda: To time the paper method on a busy day.
family: Manuel Peters is Marlowe’s half-sibling. Marlowe leaves the first voice message. Manuel calls back when there is finally a little privacy. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The crash anniversary*, Manuel says, “I was driving the other vehicle. My letter to the family has stayed in the same drawer for eleven months.”
connections: Sasha Crane. A manager timing the line hears from a customer who liked how long the conversation took.
